text:
customer_acme: Hey team — our users see SSE streams that cut off mid-response about ~10-30s into the stream. They resume with reconnect but missing the last chunk(s). Happening on our prod region eu-west-1 since 06:40 UTC. Repro guide: open stream, type prompt, sometimes final 'end-of-stream' event not delivered.

maria_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a sample request id / client logs? Also did you see any 4xx/5xx around the time?

customer_acme: request-id=rs-4b7f9a2c, trace=trace-11fc. Client logs show a socket close with ECONNRESET followed by a reconnect. No 5xx in client, but server side shows 200 then no more events.

sam_sre: Looking at our edge logs for rs-4b7f9a2c — I see upstream connection to runtime 10.2.1.7 closed mid-stream at 06:41:02. No proxy 5xx; connection reset by peer. Reconnect_rate for that customer spiked from 0.4% to 3.8% in that minute.

jonah_dev: Could be the chunked encoder on the runtime hitting a path that drops final flush. Any tcp-level captures?

customer_acme: We captured a pcap from the client side. Uploaded to secure link: https://files.redwood.test/pcaps/acme_rs4b7.pcap (internal).

maria_support: Thanks. sam—can you pull that pcap and check for FIN vs RST? If it's RST from runtime host that's suspicious.

sam_sre: Quick triage of pcap: client sends GET with 'Accept: text/event-stream' and 'Last-Event-ID' absent. Server (10.2.1.7) sends several 'data:' events then an RST from src port 443 -> client at 06:41:02. RST flagged, no FIN. That looks abrupt.

ops_ela: Also seeing a pattern in metrics: runtime CPU jumped to 92% on 10.2.1.7 and context switches spiked. Kernel OOM killer? No OOM logs, but CGROUP throttling reported.

jonah_dev: There's an old guard in the streaming code that will abort the response if the serializer sees a write error — but RST implies underlying socket drop. Could be a memory spike in handler leading to process restart. Any crash logs?

infra_bot: deploy-bot: new runtime image rolled to blue pool at 06:39 UTC for canary (image v3.2.1-rc).

sam_sre: Correlating: canary rollout coincides with incident. Hosts in that canary pool show higher reconnects. 10.2.1.7 is in the canary set.

maria_support: Customer — can you confirm if affected requests were hitting a pinned model version? Any model switches or long context lengths?

customer_acme: Yes pinned model 'gpt-tiny-2026-01' and typical seq len 1024. Not unusually long. Happens ~30% of attempts when stream is large (many incremental tokens).

jonah_dev: Repro steps I'm going to run locally: spin up runtime with v3.2.1-rc, run a client issuing SSE with long output (simulate many writes). Will add instrumentation to log each write return code and flush.

sam_sre: Meanwhile I'll pull kernel stack traces at the time window from affected host and check systemd logs. If process was OOM killed we should see coredump.

ops_ela: Also check load balancer idle timeouts and keepalive settings. If LB decides to RST after idle, client sees RST. Our LB idle is 60s but these cutoffs are at ~10-30s. Strange.

jonah_dev: I pushed a debug flag to the canary runtime to emit per-chunk write latencies and errors near 07:05. If we see 'short write' or 'broken pipe' events, that points to runtime I/O failure.

maria_support: For immediate mitigation, can you try forcing the client to use 'Connection: keep-alive' and send a heartbeat comment every 15s (':
')? That mitigates LB timeouts and can bypass kernel edge cases. Customer — can you test a heartbeat-enabled client?

customer_acme: Will test heartbeat mode and reply in 15m. Also attaching client debug logs (trimmed). Link: https://files.redwood.test/logs/acme_sse_client.log

sam_sre: Additional data: billing service reported a rate-limit error for token accounting on 06:40:58 for that request id — a 429 from internal metering. Not sure if that's related but it produced a synchronous error path in the runtime that may close connection.

jonah_dev: Good catch. There's a code path where metering 429 triggers an immediate abort with an error frame instead of graceful SSE end. If that error occurs during streaming it calls runtime.abort_with_error() which will close socket. We shouldn't RST; we should write an 'event: error' and close gracefully.

maria_support: Ticket update — root cause hypothesis: canary runtime v3.2.1-rc plus a metering 429 path caused an abrupt socket abort leading to RST observed in pcap. Action items: (1) sam to confirm process-level termination vs abort; (2) jonah to patch abort path to flush SSE error event and close with FIN; (3) ops to roll back canary if confirmed.

sam_sre: I see no coredump and the process stayed alive; kernel shows 'connection reset on write' errors. So runtime did not crash, it invoked shutdown on the socket (likely via setsockopt SO_LINGER=0 which yields RST). Need to find code path setting linger.

jonah_dev: Found it — a helper used by billing client sets SO_LINGER=0 before calling close() when it receives a non-retriable 4xx/5xx; that forces RST to avoid slow close. Will change to graceful close and emit SSE 'event: error' with JSON payload (code + message) before close. I'll open PR and request hotfix.

ops_ela: Rolling back canary to previous stable image asap. Deploy started 07:25 UTC. I'll monitor reconnect_rate and SSE truncation tickets.

customer_acme: After enabling heartbeat client, we saw much fewer truncations in the next 40 tests (down from 30% to 2%). Thanks. Will wait for your hotfix then remove heartbeat workaround.

maria_support: Great. Action summary for handoff:
- jonah_dev: PR to stop SO_LINGER=0 path and add graceful SSE error flush (link to PR in thread).
- sam_sre: validate no lingering canary pods and review kernel stats for other hosts.
- ops_ela: rollback complete, monitor metrics (reconnect_rate, stream_abort_rate, runtime_write_errors).
- customer_acme: keep heartbeat temporarily and provide any new repro pcaps if it recurs.

jonah_dev: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pull/422 — includes unit test for SSE error flush and an integration test that simulates metering 429 mid-stream.

sam_sre: Post-rollback numbers: reconnect_rate back to baseline 0.45% in eu-west-1. No RSTs in the next 30 mins of sampling.

maria_support: Closing loop with customer now. If anything else pops up, re-open thread or escalate to incidents. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:

customer_acme: Thanks all — confirm fixed for now. Will re-open if we see more.

infra_bot: alert-bot: monitor 'sse.stream_abort_rate' triggered: resolved.
